name: erg
desc: Statically typed language that can deeply improve the Python ecosystem
why: A statically typed language aimed at Python's ecosystem is unusual, though its pitch is more pragmatic than strange.

brief.what_it_is: Erg is a statically typed programming language whose compiler lives in this repository, along with its documentation. It takes Erg source files (.er) and checks them at compile time, using a type system with dependent and refinement types, so errors like out-of-range list indexing or unit mismatches are reported before running. The README's examples run through Python, and it also ships a REPL and an Erg Language Server (ELS, behind a feature flag). The README does not spell out the output format, so treat the exact artifacts it produces as unstated.
brief.why_it_exists: The README pitches Erg at people who want Rust-like robustness without Rust's verbose type specifications and memory management, and at people who are frustrated with Python but cannot throw away their Python code. It also names an ML-style simplicity goal and a Scala-style blend of object-oriented and functional programming.
brief.how_it_works: The README does not describe the compiler's internals. It says Erg is internally compatible with Python and imports Python modules with the pyimport keyword, which it claims works at zero cost. Side effects are marked with a trailing ! on names and methods, and the compiler rejects calling a procedural method inside a function.

brief.install_notes: A Python 3 interpreter is required, the README says 3.7 to 3.11, and if Python is already installed no setup is needed. Building from source needs the Rust toolchain; Nix users can use nix-build or nix build with Flakes enabled. Optional cargo feature flags include --features japanese, simplified_chinese, or traditional_chinese for localized error messages; els for the language server; full-repl for a richer REPL; unicode and pretty for nicer display; and full to enable everything except developer-only features. No accounts or runtime configuration beyond these are mentioned.
brief.standout: Most languages that target Python bolt types on afterward, but Erg puts dependent and refinement types, compile-time index and unit checks, and a ! marker for side effects into a Python-compatible language. The error messages are also unusually detailed, with hints pointing to the mutable variant of a method.
brief.status: The README has a release badge, a CI build-status badge, and a Discord link, but gives no release date, version number, or last-commit date, so the maintenance state is unknown from these pages. The README says some features are not yet implemented and refers to TODO.md for status, which I did not fetch.
brief.caveats: The README says some features are not yet implemented, with status in TODO.md. It requires Python 3.7 to 3.11 at runtime. Building from source requires the Rust toolchain. The license is split: Apache 2.0 plus MIT for code, and CC-BY-4.0 for the assets and doc folders. The homepage was reachable.

entry.title: Erg
entry.tldr: A statically typed language that runs on Python, with refinement types that catch out-of-range indexes and unit mismatches at compile time.
entry.deeper_look:
Erg is a programming language whose compiler checks `.er` source files before anything runs. Its type system includes dependent and refinement types, so mistakes like indexing past the end of a list or mixing up units are reported at compile time. It also ships a REPL and an optional language server, ELS, behind a feature flag.

The README pitches it at two groups. One wants Rust-like robustness without Rust's verbose type annotations and memory management. The other is frustrated with Python but cannot throw away its Python code. The README also names an ML-style simplicity goal and a Scala-style mix of object-oriented and functional programming.

Erg is described as internally compatible with Python. Python modules come in through the `pyimport` keyword, which the README says works "at zero cost". Side effects are marked with a trailing `!` on names and methods, and the compiler rejects calling a procedural method inside a function. The README says error messages are a priority, with hints such as pointing you to the mutable variant of a method.

The idea underneath is that a type system can carry more than "this is an int". Ranges, units and purity become things the compiler checks. Erg lets you try that on top of an ecosystem you already know.
entry.install:
brew install erg
# A Python 3 interpreter is required (README says 3.7 to 3.11).
# From source instead: cargo install erg (needs the Rust toolchain). Optional feature flags include els, full-repl, and full.

try_this.what_happens: Lists the available commands and options for the compiler.
With no arguments, the README's REPL is the place to try expressions and see type errors immediately.

entry.whats_unique: Most languages that target Python bolt types on afterward. Erg builds refinement and dependent types, compile-time index and unit checks, and a `!` marker for side effects into a Python-compatible language.
entry.caveats: The README says some features are not yet implemented, it requires Python 3.7 to 3.11 at runtime, and it gives no release or last-commit date, so maintenance state is unclear.
